unit.title: The Kitchen
unit.summary: The non-volley zone: volleys, the line, momentum, when you may enter.

lessons.title: What the kitchen is
lessons.objective: Define the non-volley zone and its line.

payload.prompt: Match kitchen terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: The 7-foot no-volley zone on each side of the net where you cannot hit the ball in the air
The official name for the kitchen; the restricted area for volleys
The boundary at the back edge of the kitchen; counts as part of the kitchen

distractorDefinitions: The service box where you stand to serve
The area you must reach to win a point

explanation.summary: The kitchen is the 7-foot strip on each side of the net where volleys are forbidden. It's called the non-volley zone (NVZ) officially. The kitchen line marks its back boundary and counts as kitchen.
explanation.sayThisLine: The kitchen is the 7-foot no-volley zone on each side.

payload.prompt: How far from the net is the kitchen on each side?

options.text: 3 feet
7 feet
10 feet
15 feet

explanation.correct: The kitchen is exactly 7 feet from the net on each side. That's 14 feet from baseline to baseline in the kitchen zones.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen is always 7 feet. That standard distance keeps the game balanced: far enough that you can't just smash from the net, close enough to matter.
explanation.sayThisLine: The kitchen is 7 feet from the net on each side.

payload.prompt: Complete the kitchen definition.
payload.template: The kitchen is a {{area}} zone {{distance}} from the net on {{sides}}.

explanation.correct: The kitchen is a no-volley zone, 7 feet from the net, on each side. You can stand in it and hit bounced balls; you just can't volley.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen is on both sides of the net (not just one), exactly 7 feet deep, and named for the no-volley rule that applies there.
explanation.sayThisLine: 7-foot no-volley zone, each side of the net.

payload.prompt: A ball bounces 8 feet from the net; the kitchen line is at 7 feet. Where does it land?

scene.alt: Top-down court view showing a ball landing 8 feet from the net, past the kitchen line.

explanation.correct: Out of the kitchen. The kitchen extends 7 feet from the net; anything past that is outside. You can volley that ball.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen is only 7 feet deep. A ball landing 8 feet from the net is past the kitchen line, so it's in open court.
explanation.sayThisLine: Ball past the kitchen line is in play for volleys.

lessons.title: What is a volley?
lessons.objective: Distinguish a volley from a groundstroke.

payload.prompt: What makes a shot a volley?

options.text: You hit it hard and fast
You hit it before it bounces
You stand near the net
You use a certain grip

explanation.correct: A volley is any shot hit in the air before the ball bounces. The ball doesn't touch the court before you strike it.
explanation.incorrect: Volleying is defined by the timing: the ball is still in flight when you hit it. Speed, position, and grip don't define it.
explanation.sayThisLine: A volley is hitting the ball in the air before it bounces.

payload.prompt: The ball bounces 2 feet away. You step in and hit it before the bounce completes.

scene.alt: You stand in the court with a ball in flight approaching, not yet bounced.

explanation.correct: Volley. The ball hasn't bounced yet; you're hitting it in the air. That's the definition.
explanation.incorrect: If the ball hasn't bounced when you hit it, it's a volley. A groundstroke only counts if you let it bounce first.
explanation.sayThisLine: Hit it in the air = volley. After a bounce = groundstroke.

payload.prompt: A soft dink floats toward you. Should you volley or let it bounce?

situation.narrative: You're at the kitchen line. A dink float is coming toward you, still in the air.

facts.label: Your position
facts.value: At the kitchen line, outside the kitchen

options.label: Volley it now, in the air
options.consequence: A volley here is legal because you're outside the kitchen. A waist-high dink is easy to volley softly back.
considerations: You're in legal position (outside the kitchen)
Volleying a float requires a soft touch
A volley gives you immediate control

options.label: Let it bounce and then hit it
options.consequence: Letting it bounce gives you a better angle and more time to position. Groundstrokes on bounced dinks are easier to control.
considerations: Bounced balls are easier to read
You can adjust your feet before hitting
Soft dinks often land short anyway, giving you options

payload.expertNote: Both work; bouncing gives you more control and time. Volleying is riskier with a soft floater.
payload.sayThisLine: Let soft dinks bounce when you can; easier to control.

payload.prompt: Complete the volley definition.
payload.template: A volley is a shot where the ball is hit {{when}} it {{touches}}.

explanation.correct: A volley is hit before the ball touches the court. Once it bounces, any shot is a groundstroke or a return.
explanation.incorrect: The key to a volley is that the ball never bounces. You strike it in the air, before impact with the court.
explanation.sayThisLine: Volley = hit before bounce. Groundstroke = hit after bounce.

lessons.title: No volleys in the kitchen
lessons.objective: Call fair vs faulty volleys with feet on court.

payload.prompt: You are standing with both feet in the kitchen and you volley the ball.

scene.alt: You stand with feet inside the kitchen zone, volleying a ball.

explanation.correct: Kitchen fault. You cannot volley while standing in the kitchen, no matter how good the shot looks.
explanation.incorrect: The rule is simple: no volleys in the kitchen, period. Your feet position determines it, and both are in the zone.
explanation.sayThisLine: Feet in the kitchen = no volley. That's a fault.

payload.prompt: You stand just outside the kitchen and volley. Is that legal?

options.text: No, you are still near the kitchen
Yes, if your feet are outside the kitchen line
Only if the ball is above the net
Only on your first volley

explanation.correct: Legal. The rule is about foot position: if both feet are outside the kitchen line, you can volley anywhere on the court.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen volley rule cares only about where your feet are at the moment of contact. Outside the line = legal volley.
explanation.sayThisLine: Feet outside the kitchen = legal to volley.

payload.prompt: Match the foot position to the call.

pairs.definition: Kitchen fault; you cannot volley from there

pairs.term: One foot in, one foot out
pairs.definition: Kitchen fault; any part of your body in the kitchen means no volley
Legal to volley; foot position is clear

distractorDefinitions: Legal only if the ball is below the net
Legal only if it is a soft shot

explanation.summary: Kitchen faults happen when any part of your feet touches the kitchen line or is inside the zone when you volley. Both feet outside is the only legal position to volley.
explanation.sayThisLine: Any foot in the kitchen = fault. Both out = legal.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: I was standing in the kitchen and I hit a perfect volley. They called it a fault.

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: That's the rule: no volleys in the kitchen, even perfect ones.
If it was perfect, it should count.
They probably missaw your foot position.
The kitchen rule is too strict.

payload.translation: The kitchen volley rule is absolute: your feet position, not the shot quality, determines legality. Foot in the kitchen = fault, no exceptions.

followUps.line: The kitchen rule doesn't care how good the shot is. Feet in the zone, it's a fault.
followUps.why: Affirms the rule and her understanding.

followUps.line: Volleys need the feet outside. That's the whole point of the kitchen.
followUps.why: Explains the strategy behind the rule.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: The kitchen volley rule is non-negotiable; don't defend a kitchen fault.

lessons.title: The line counts as kitchen
lessons.objective: Recognize a toe on the line as in the kitchen.

payload.prompt: Tap the area where a volley fault occurs if your foot lands there.

diagram.alt: Top-down pickleball court showing the kitchen zones and the kitchen line.

explanation.correct: Both the line and the interior are kitchen. A foot on the line, or inside it, means you cannot volley from there.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen line is part of the kitchen for volley rules. Touching the line with your foot is the same as being inside.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen line counts as kitchen when volleying.

payload.prompt: Your toe touches the kitchen line and you volley.

scene.alt: You stand with one toe touching the kitchen line, volleying the ball.

explanation.correct: Kitchen fault. The line itself counts as kitchen. A toe on the line is the same as a foot in the zone.
explanation.incorrect: Many people think the line is safe, but it isn't. For volley rules, the line = kitchen.
explanation.sayThisLine: Toe on the kitchen line = kitchen fault.

payload.ruleTag: Kitchen line is part of the kitchen

payload.prompt: If your foot is exactly on the kitchen line and you volley, is it legal?

options.text: Yes, the line itself is neutral territory
No, the line counts as kitchen for volleys
Only if you're moving backward
Only if the ball is above your head

explanation.correct: The line counts as kitchen. A foot touching the line is a kitchen fault when volleying.
explanation.incorrect: Unlike some sports, in pickleball the kitchen line is not a neutral boundary. It's part of the kitchen.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen line counts as kitchen; touching it = fault when volleying.

payload.prompt: During a volley rally, you need to move forward. Where should your foot land?

situation.narrative: A ball is coming toward the kitchen. You need to advance to volley it.

facts.label: Foot landing option
facts.value: Exactly on the kitchen line vs. clearly in open court

options.label: Advance your foot to land on the kitchen line
options.consequence: Kitchen fault. The line is kitchen, so your foot position is illegal when you volley.
considerations: The line itself counts as kitchen
You will lose the rally with a fault
Risk is too high

options.label: Advance fully past the line into open court, then volley
options.consequence: Legal. Both feet clearly past the line, you can volley safely. The risk of a kitchen fault is gone.
considerations: Clear foot position = no doubt
You control the rally
Safety first when near the line

payload.expertNote: When advancing in a volley rally, go all the way past the kitchen line. Straddling it is a fault waiting to happen.
payload.sayThisLine: Past the line to volley. Straddling the line = fault.

lessons.title: The momentum trap
lessons.objective: Judge a volley followed by momentum into the zone.

payload.prompt: You volley from outside the kitchen, but your forward momentum carries your foot into the zone after you hit the ball.

scene.alt: You are shown volleying from outside the kitchen, with an arrow indicating your forward momentum.

explanation.correct: Momentum fault. Even if you start outside the kitchen, if your momentum carries you in after the volley, it's a fault.
explanation.incorrect: The momentum rule prevents players from using forward force to avoid the kitchen boundary. Your position after contact matters.
explanation.sayThisLine: Momentum into the kitchen after volleying = fault.

payload.prompt: Why does the momentum rule exist?

options.text: To prevent hard smashes at the net
To stop players from using forward force to cheat the kitchen boundary
To slow down aggressive play
To protect the court surface

explanation.correct: The momentum rule prevents players from stepping outside the kitchen, volleying, and then letting their body carry them into the zone. It's the integrity of the boundary.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen has a boundary. The momentum rule enforces that boundary even when a player's natural motion would take them into it.
explanation.sayThisLine: Momentum rule keeps the kitchen boundary honest.

payload.prompt: You are outside the kitchen preparing to volley an incoming ball. Should you be aggressive or cautious?

situation.narrative: A ball is coming toward the kitchen line. You are 1 foot outside the line, ready to volley.

facts.label: Shot opportunity
facts.value: A short volley that you could attack hard

facts.label: Risk
facts.value: Your momentum could carry you into the zone

options.label: Attack hard with full momentum forward
options.consequence: High risk of a momentum fault. A hard forward swing will likely carry you into the kitchen after contact.
considerations: Kitchen momentum faults are easy to call
You're only 1 foot away
An aggressive finish is dangerous here

options.label: Take a controlled, soft volley without leaning in
options.consequence: Safe and legal. A softer swing keeps your momentum under control and your feet out of the kitchen.
considerations: Controlled volleys are neutral or good
You stay safely outside the kitchen
You're protecting yourself from a fault

payload.expertNote: When volleying near the kitchen line, stay compact and controlled. Aggressive swings lead to momentum faults.
payload.sayThisLine: Soft volley near the line; hard swing risks momentum fault.

lessons.title: When you can go in
lessons.objective: Know you may enter to hit a bounced ball; must exit before volleying.

payload.prompt: A ball bounces in the kitchen. Can you go in to hit it?

situation.narrative: Your opponent hits a short shot that lands in your kitchen and bounces.

facts.label: Your action
facts.value: Entering the zone to reach it

options.label: Enter the kitchen and hit the bounced ball
options.consequence: Totally legal. You can enter the kitchen to hit bounced balls. The kitchen rule only forbids volleys, not groundstrokes.
considerations: Bounced balls are always fair to hit
You can stand in the kitchen if the ball bounced there
This is smart offensive play

options.label: Stay back and let it bounce again
options.consequence: You can do this, but you lose position. Entering to hit the bounce is the aggressive play.
considerations: Staying back gives you less control
You lose the point position
Entering is the better strategy

payload.expertNote: If a ball bounces in the kitchen, go get it. You have the right to enter the zone for a bounced ball.
payload.sayThisLine: Ball bounces in the kitchen? You can go in to hit it.

payload.prompt: You are in the kitchen, ball bounces outside, floats back. You volley from inside.

scene.alt: You stand inside the kitchen zone, volleying a ball that bounced outside.

explanation.correct: Kitchen fault. You can enter the kitchen to hit a bounced ball, but you must exit before volleying again.
explanation.incorrect: The rule is clear: if you are in the kitchen, no volleys. You have to leave the zone before you can volley the next shot.
explanation.sayThisLine: In the kitchen? Hit groundstrokes only. Leave before volleying.

payload.prompt: You are in the kitchen after a bounce. What can you do?

options.text: Volley the next ball that comes to you
Hit only groundstrokes and then leave the zone
Stay there and wait for instructions
Hit any shot, then move back

explanation.correct: You can hit groundstrokes in the kitchen (bounced balls), but before you volley again, you must exit the zone.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen is only open for groundstrokes once you're in it. Volleys are not allowed from inside; you must leave first.
explanation.sayThisLine: In the kitchen: hit bounces, then exit before volleying.

payload.prompt: Complete the kitchen entry rule.
payload.template: You may enter the kitchen to hit a {{ball-type}} ball, but you must {{action}} before volleying.

explanation.correct: You can enter the kitchen for a bounced ball, but you must leave the zone before you can volley again.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen rule allows groundstrokes inside but forbids volleys. Exit, then volley.
explanation.sayThisLine: Bounce in kitchen? Go in. But exit before volleying again.

lessons.title: Reaching over
lessons.objective: Know paddle over the zone is fine if feet are outside.

payload.prompt: You stand outside the kitchen with both feet clear. Your paddle reaches over the kitchen line to volley.

scene.alt: You stand outside the kitchen while your paddle extends over the kitchen line to hit the ball.

explanation.correct: Legal. Your paddle can reach over the kitchen as long as your feet are outside the zone. Only foot position matters.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen rule is about foot position, not paddle reach. As long as your feet are out, your paddle can go anywhere.
explanation.sayThisLine: Paddle over kitchen is fine; feet outside = legal.

payload.ruleTag: Paddle reaching over kitchen is legal

payload.prompt: What part of your body matters for the kitchen volley rule?

options.text: Your paddle position
Your arm or hand
Your foot position
Your balance

explanation.correct: Foot position is the only thing that matters for the kitchen volley rule. Paddle and arms can reach over; feet must stay out.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen rule is about where your feet are when you volley, not where your paddle or hands reach.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen rule is about feet, not paddle. Paddle can reach over.

payload.prompt: Match the body part to whether it can enter the kitchen for a volley.

pairs.definition: Cannot be in or touching the kitchen line when volleying; this causes a fault
Can reach over or into the kitchen freely when volleying; no restriction
Can reach over the kitchen as much as needed; only feet are restricted

distractorDefinitions: Can only reach over the kitchen once per rally
Must stay behind the baseline at all times

explanation.summary: The kitchen volley rule applies only to feet. Your paddle, arm and hand can reach freely over the zone. It's about foot placement.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen rule: feet can't be in. Paddle and arm: reach away.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: I had to reach my paddle over the kitchen to volley. Was that a fault?

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: No, paddle reach is fine. What matters is where your feet are.
Yeah, you can't reach over the kitchen.
Only if you stepped in too.
It depends on the angle of your paddle.

payload.translation: Paddle reaching over the kitchen is perfectly legal. The kitchen rule cares only about foot position, not reach.

followUps.line: Paddle can go anywhere. The kitchen rule is just about where your feet are.
followUps.why: Direct and clears up the confusion.

followUps.line: As long as your feet were outside the kitchen, the volley is legal.
followUps.why: Focuses on the actual rule: foot position.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: This is a common misconception. Paddle reach is always legal; feet position is what matters.

lessons.title: Why the kitchen exists
lessons.objective: Explain the zone's purpose (no smashes at the net).

payload.prompt: Complete the reason for the kitchen.
payload.template: The kitchen exists to prevent players from {{action}} at the net, which would {{consequence}}.

explanation.correct: The kitchen prevents net players from smashing weak balls away. Without it, whoever reaches the net first would win every rally.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen creates a balanced game by forcing net players to dink soft. Soft play keeps rallies alive.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen stops net smashes; it keeps the game balanced.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: Why can't I just rush the net and smash everything? I'm good at the net.

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: That's what the kitchen is for: to keep net dominance from ending rallies.
You're not as good at the net as you think.
The kitchen rule is unfair to good volleyers.
Smashing is not allowed in pickleball.

payload.translation: The kitchen forces net players to be soft and patient. It's the reason soft game and dinking strategy matter. Without it, pickleball would be a serve-and-volley race to the net.

followUps.line: That's where the kitchen comes in. Without it, net players would dominate. The soft game is what makes pickleball interesting.
The kitchen makes it a game of patience and angles, not just reaching the net.
followUps.why: Describes what the kitchen does for the sport.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: The kitchen is the heart of pickleball strategy. It's not a limitation; it's the reason the game works.

payload.prompt: What would happen to pickleball if there were no kitchen?

options.text: The game would be slower
Whoever reached the net first would smash and win
Soft shots would become more common
Serves would matter less

explanation.correct: Without the kitchen, net dominance wins. The first player to reach the net could volley away every ball with an unreturnable smash.
explanation.incorrect: The kitchen makes pickleball unique: it forces patience and soft play instead of power. Removing it would turn it into tennis.
explanation.sayThisLine: No kitchen = whoever reaches the net smashes and wins every point.

payload.prompt: You are at the net with a ball at your feet. Why should you dink instead of smashing?

situation.narrative: Your opponent sent a weak dink to the net. You are at the kitchen line and you could smash it.

facts.label: Your position
facts.value: At the net, in the kitchen

options.label: Smash it hard (if you could)
options.consequence: Smashing at the net would end every rally instantly. The game would reward net dominance alone, not strategy or skill.
considerations: Without the kitchen, power would rule
Soft play and angles would be pointless
Pickleball would become just about reaching the net

options.label: Dink soft (per the kitchen rule)
options.consequence: Dinking keeps the rally alive and forces your opponent to be patient. It's the heart of pickleball strategy and why the game is fun.
considerations: Dinking is the counter-strategy to the kitchen
It tests patience and angles, not just power
It's what separates pickleball from power sports

payload.expertNote: The kitchen makes dinking mandatory at the net. That's the whole point: soft play beats power in pickleball.
payload.sayThisLine: Kitchen forces soft play. That's what makes pickleball special.
